newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus grain harvest to rise to 6.5 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Belarus grain harvest to rise to 6.5 mln tonnes.

text.p: Belarus has nearly completed its grain harvest, with total output this year to rise to 6.5 million tonnes, a top agriculture official said on Thursday.
"We are almost finished and should have 6.5 million tonnes," Deputy Agriculture Minister Ivan Shokolo told Reuters.
Belarus harvested 5.6 million tonnes of grain last year.
Shokolo said state sector output would be six million tonnes, and private sector production would be 500,000 tonnes.
Only maize was left to be harvested, he said.
Grain yields were 2.5 tonnes per hectare.

Agriculture Minister Vasily Leoniv said this week that Belarus would buy about 500,000 tonnes of wheat this year, most likely from Ukraine. He said the wheat would not be purchased all at once but in several parcels.
President Alexander Lukashenko said during meetings this week with agriculture sector representatives that Belarus's goal was to eliminate imports altogether.
"Our task in the next three years is to completely do without imports," he told national television earlier this week.
The former Soviet republic imported one million tonnes of grain last year, mostly other ex-Soviet republics. --Larisa Sayenko, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
